%d containers are open. Their files can be read in other apps.

resources.string: No known signature, so it is offered as a VeraCrypt volume. Enter its password and PIM.
This is a LUKS volume (LUKS1 or LUKS2). Enter its password.
This is a ZIP archive. It opens without a password, read-only.
This is an AES Crypt file (version 2). Enter its password; the file is checked whole before it opens.
This is an ISO 9660 disc image. It opens without a password, read-only.
Lock when the screen turns off

After a container opens, its password is saved under your phone\'s lock. When you pick the same file again, your fingerprint or screen lock opens it. This needs a screen lock (PIN, pattern or password).
The saved password no longer opens this container, so it was forgotten. Type the new one.
The saved password could not be read. Type it instead.
Opened. The password was not saved, because this phone has no screen lock.
Open VeraCrypt and LUKS containers read-only. Turn it off to add, change and delete the files inside them. ZIP, ISO and AES Crypt files always open read-only.
This is a TAR archive. It opens without a password, read-only.
This is a gzip-compressed TAR archive. It opens without a password, read-only.
This is a 7z archive. Enter its password if it has one. It opens read-only.
This is a restic repository. Enter its password. Its snapshots open read-only, one folder each.
This is a macOS disk image. It opens read-only. Enter a password only if the APFS volume inside is encrypted.
